analyst_view.overall: Early view: Palladino's Bologna have won four in a row and Orsolini is back from injury, scoring the winning penalty at Parma, though Miranda went off injured in that game. Udinese are bottom with one point from five games and, according to Tuttomercatoweb, have already replaced Runjaic with Paolo Zanetti. Neither side has a European game to worry about.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals. I lean higher: Bologna are in form and had 33 shots at Parma, while Udinese have let in 2.2 goals a game away and 25 in total. Udinese's new coach has had little time to fix the defence, and striker Davis has yet to score in the league, which keeps this mostly about Bologna.

corners.text: The site expects 9.5 corners. Bologna's home games average about 10.6 and Udinese's away games about 8.6, which lands right on the number. Bologna's wide pairs such as Cambiaghi and Orsolini do produce corners, but I see no strong reason to move.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards. Bologna's home games have been among the most card-heavy in the league, at almost six on average, while Udinese's away games have been very calm. These pull in opposite directions, so I stay with the number until the referee is known.

shots.text: The site expects 26.2 shots. I lean slightly higher: Udinese allow about 15.5 shots a game and Bologna's attack is in form, with Orsolini, Bernardeschi and Odgaard all providing shots. Udinese also take more than 13 shots a game away, so this should not be one-way.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 shots on target. I lean higher because Udinese concede 6.2 shots on target a game, the second-worst figure in Serie A, and their away games have averaged nearly ten. A team in front of a new coach is often slow to fix that.
